meta.note: Baseline snapshot for downstream (vllm-ascend) commit-impact analysis. Interface signatures anchored to this commit.

project_overview.what: vLLM is a high-throughput, memory-efficient LLM inference and serving engine. It implements PagedAttention for KV-cache management, continuous batching, tensor/pipeline/expert parallelism, and an OpenAI-compatible server.
problems_solved: KV-cache memory fragmentation and waste (PagedAttention block management)
Low GPU utilization from static batching (continuous batching scheduler)
Hardware portability: a platform abstraction lets out-of-tree (OOT) accelerators plug in
Compilation overhead: torch.compile + CUDA graph capture with piecewise partitioning
Model breadth: hundreds of architectures via a lazy registry
project_overview.architecture_style: Layered: entrypoints -> engine (front-end LLMEngine + inner EngineCore loop) -> executor -> worker/model_runner -> model_executor layers -> attention backends/kernels. Platform abstraction is a cross-cutting seam; OOT platforms inject via entry points and subclass stable base classes.
project_overview.key_design_principle: v1 split: front-end (EngineCoreClient/LLMEngine) is decoupled from the inner EngineCore loop over ZMQ; Worker executes the model; Scheduler owns KV-cache allocation. Stable base classes are the plugin contract; concrete CUDA/ROCm/XPU implementations are not.

core_modules.responsibility: Hardware abstraction. Device discovery, capability queries, attention-backend selection, block-size alignment, communicator/compile/punica class resolution, config defaulting.
core_modules.implementation_principle: `Platform` is a duck-typed base (not ABC); unsupported ops raise NotImplementedError. Current platform is detected lazily via `resolve_current_platform_cls_qualname()`, which chains builtin plugins (tpu/cuda/rocm/xpu/cpu) with OOT plugins loaded from the `vllm.platform_plugins` entry-point group. Exactly one OOT plugin may activate. `current_platform` is resolved lazily via module `__getattr__` to avoid import cycles.

core_modules.responsibility: Engine front-end (LLMEngine, AsyncLLM) and inner EngineCore loop; EngineCoreClient transports (inproc/sync-mp/async-mp, DP variants); input/output processing.
core_modules.implementation_principle: LLMEngine.step() calls engine_core.get_output(); EngineCore.step() runs scheduler.schedule -> executor.execute_model(non_block) -> scheduler.get_grammar_bitmask -> executor.sample_tokens (if execute_model returned None) -> scheduler.update_from_output. The execute/sample split lets structured-output grammar computation overlap.

core_modules.responsibility: Scheduling and KV-cache coordination. Decides which requests to run each step, token budgets, preemption, chunked prefill, spec-decode token scheduling.
core_modules.implementation_principle: SchedulerInterface (ABC) -> Scheduler (concrete). schedule() selects requests, allocates blocks via KVCacheManager, returns SchedulerOutput (new cached reqs + token counts). update_from_output() consumes ModelRunnerOutput, advances request state, frees/allocates blocks. AsyncScheduler overrides hooks for async scheduling.

core_modules.responsibility: Attention backend selection and implementations (FlashAttention, FlashInfer, Triton, FlashMLA, ROCm AITER, CPU, XPU, MLA prefill backends).
core_modules.implementation_principle: Selector (AttentionSelectorConfig -> get_attn_backend) queries `current_platform.get_attn_backend_cls(...)`, which validates candidates against device capability and picks the highest-priority valid backend, returning a class-path string resolved via resolve_obj_by_qualname. Result is cached (`@cache`). Backends declare capabilities via supports_* classmethods and validate_configuration. Registration via AttentionBackendEnum + register_backend.

core_modules.responsibility: Worker (device control-plane) and ModelRunner (model execution). Device init, memory profiling for KV-cache sizing, weight loading, CUDA graph capture, forward execution, sampling.
core_modules.implementation_principle: WorkerBase declares the override surface; GPU Worker (subclass) implements init_device/determine_available_memory/initialize_from_config/execute_model. GPUModelRunner.execute_model builds attention metadata, runs the model forward, computes logits, stores ExecuteModelState and returns None; sample_tokens() consumes that state to sample. Platform plugins subclass Worker and override `_make_model_runner`; ModelRunner override points are `_model_forward`, `_init_device_properties`, `_sync_device`, `_on_request_state_removed`.

core_modules.responsibility: torch.compile integration: compiler adaptors (Inductor standalone/inductor/eager), custom graph splitting, piecewise compilation, CUDA-graph wrapping, Inductor passes (fusion, noop elimination).
core_modules.implementation_principle: CompilationConfig.init_backend() returns either a stock torch backend string or a VllmBackend instance (VLLM_COMPILE mode). VllmBackend partitions the graph by splitting_ops into submodules (PiecewiseCompileInterpreter), compiles each via CompilerManager -> CompilerInterface, and optionally wraps with AbstractStaticGraphWrapper (CUDA graphs). PostGradPassManager runs registered Inductor passes. Compile cache keyed by config hash + compiler hash + traced-code hash.

core_modules.responsibility: Distributed primitives: world/TP/PP/DP/EP/DCP/PCP group management, device communicators (NCCL, custom all-reduce, all2all), KV/EC transfer connectors, weight transfer.
core_modules.implementation_principle: GroupCoordinator wraps a torch ProcessGroup + optional DeviceCommunicatorBase (resolved via platform.get_device_communicator_cls()). initialize_model_parallel builds groups with rank layout ExternalDP x DP x PP x PCP x TP. All2All backends (DeepEP, MoonEP, FlashInfer, etc.) implement All2AllManagerBase for MoE dispatch/combine.

core_modules.responsibility: Model definitions, layer implementations (attention/linear/MoE/quantization/rotary), model registry, weight loading.
core_modules.implementation_principle: ModelRegistry lazily resolves arch -> class, caching _ModelInfo. Layers are CustomOp/PluggableLayer subclasses dispatchable per-platform (forward_cuda/hip/xpu/cpu/oot) and OOT-overridable via register_oot. Quantization methods and linear kernels are selected per platform+quant config.

core_modules.responsibility: KV-cache specification hierarchy and runtime block management.
core_modules.implementation_principle: KVCacheSpec (frozen dataclass) describes per-layer cache geometry; KVCacheManager owns a BlockPool (hash-based prefix caching, free queue) and a KVCacheCoordinator (unitary/hybrid/no-prefix) that maps requests to blocks. Custom specs/managers register via @register_kv_cache_spec.

core_modules.responsibility: Token sampling: logits processors, temperature/top-k/top-p, rejection sampling for speculative decode.
core_modules.implementation_principle: Sampler (nn.Module) computes logprobs, applies logits processors, delegates stochastic sampling to TopKTopPSampler whose `forward` is bound per-platform (cuda/cpu/hip/xpu/native). RejectionSampler implements spec-decode acceptance.

@config decorator wraps pydantic dataclass; VllmConfig aggregates sub-configs; compute_hash() drives compile cache; Platform.check_and_update_config()/apply_config_platform_defaults() mutate config for a platform.

core_modules.responsibility: User-facing APIs: offline LLM class, OpenAI/Anthropic/Cohere-compatible servers, CLI.
core_modules.implementation_principle: LLM composes offline mixins (generate/chat/embed/classify/score/beam_search). Server startup in launchers/api_server builds AsyncLLM from VllmConfig via AsyncEngineArgs.

implementation_principles.detail: `vllm/platforms/__init__.py` loads the `vllm.platform_plugins` entry-point group via `load_plugins_by_group`. Each entry point is a factory returning either a platform class qualname or None. Builtins (tpu/cuda/rocm/xpu/cpu) are chained with OOT plugins; exactly one OOT may activate, else RuntimeError. `current_platform` is resolved lazily through module-level `__getattr__` (avoids import cycles because OOT plugins import `Platform` from vllm.platforms). vllm-ascend registers a `vllm.platform_plugins` entry point returning `vllm_ascend.platform.NPUPlatform`.

LLMEngine.step() -> EngineCoreClient.get_output() -> (InprocClient) EngineCore.step_fn() where step_fn is step or step_with_batch_queue. EngineCore.step: scheduler.schedule(throttle) -> SchedulerOutput; executor.execute_model(scheduler_output, non_block=True) -> future; scheduler.get_grammar_bitmask(scheduler_output) computed in parallel; future.result() -> ModelRunnerOutput or None; if None, executor.sample_tokens(grammar_output); _process_aborts_queue(); scheduler.update_from_output(scheduler_output, model_output) -> per-engine EngineCoreOutputs; returns (outputs, model_executed).

execute_model returns None after doing all model work (this is the async-scheduling seam). Steps: validate execute_model_state empty -> handle KV-connector preemptions -> _update_states (persistent batch) -> early-return for EC/empty -> _prepare_inputs (logits_indices, spec-decode metadata) -> determine batch execution/padding & cudagraph mode -> _get_slot_mappings -> _build_attention_metadata -> _preprocess (input_ids/positions/model_kwargs) -> _model_forward under set_forward_context -> postprocess (PP intermediate, pooling, or compute logits) -> store ExecuteModelState -> return None. Then sample_tokens() unpacks state, applies grammar bitmask, samples, updates states, proposes draft tokens, returns ModelRunnerOutput. Override points: _model_forward, _init_device_properties, _sync_device, _on_request_state_removed; Worker._make_model_runner selects the runner class.

Attention.__init__ (or layer) calls selector.get_attn_backend(...), which builds an AttentionSelectorConfig, applies attention_config.backend_per_kind overrides, and calls the cached _cached_get_attn_backend. That delegates to current_platform.get_attn_backend_cls(selected_backend, attn_selector_config, num_heads), which returns a class-path string. CUDA's implementation validates each candidate via backend_cls.validate_configuration(device_capability=..., **selector._asdict()) and picks the highest-priority valid backend, logging invalid reasons. The string is resolved via resolve_obj_by_qualname. OOT platforms override get_attn_backend_cls to return their own backend; backends can also be registered/overridden via AttentionBackendEnum.register() / register_backend().

CompilationConfig.init_backend() returns a stock backend string for STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE/DYNAMO_TRACE_ONCE, or a VllmBackend instance for VLLM_COMPILE. VllmBackend splits the fx graph on splitting_ops into piecewise submodules (PiecewiseCompileInterpreter), compiles each via CompilerManager -> CompilerInterface.compile (InductorAdaptor / InductorStandaloneAdaptor / platform backend), and optionally wraps pieces with AbstractStaticGraphWrapper for CUDA graphs. PostGradPassManager runs custom Inductor passes (fusion, noop elimination) and is installed under Platform.pass_key ('post_grad_custom_post_pass'). Compile cache key = VllmConfig hash + compiler hash + traced-code hash.

At startup, each attention layer reports get_kv_cache_spec(); specs are grouped into KVCacheGroups (KVCacheConfig). KVCacheManager builds a BlockPool (all blocks, free queue, hash->block map) and a KVCacheCoordinator (unitary/hybrid/no-prefix). During schedule(), allocate_slots() maps a request's tokens to blocks (with prefix-cache hash matching), and the scheduler records block_ids in ScheduledNewReqs/CachedReqs. The worker initializes physical KV tensors (initialize_kv_cache) and attention metadata builders consume block tables. Prefix caching is hash-based at hash_block_size granularity.

init_distributed_environment creates the world group; initialize_model_parallel builds TP/PP/DP/EP/DCP/PCP/EPLB groups (rank order ExternalDP x DP x PP x PCP x TP). GroupCoordinator wraps each ProcessGroup and lazily constructs a DeviceCommunicatorBase resolved from current_platform.get_device_communicator_cls(). MoE all2all uses All2AllManagerBase implementations selected by all2all_backend. Weight/KV/EC transfer use dedicated connectors.

Platform-specific behavior is centralized in Platform subclasses (cuda/rocm/xpu/cpu/tpu/zen_cpu + OOT). Examples: CUDA selects attention via device capability priorities and enables custom all-reduce + opaque attention op; ROCm overrides attention/quantization and uses AITER; XPU provides custom sampler/attention; CPU disables cudagraph and custom all-reduce. Common platform-agnostic seams: get_attn_backend_cls, get_device_communicator_cls, get_punica_wrapper, import_kernels, register_triton_kernel_overrides, compile backend/pass manager, supported_dtypes, supported_quantization.
